issues.description: The Rideable.messageOnRide method is specified and used as a no-argument method in the problem statement and template (and the UML shows messageOnRide():String). However, the solution repository defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) and the implementing classes (Seal, Pig) implement messageOnRide(int speed). This parameter mismatch means the solution does not match the specified interface and the template/main usage (which calls messageOnRide() with no arguments), and would confuse students about the correct method signature to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method signature across all artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to match the specification and template by making Rideable.messageOnRide() a no-argument method and update Seal and Pig implementations to messageOnRide() returning "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]", or (B) update the problem statement and template to specify a parameter (e.g. int speed) and adjust usages accordingly. Prefer option (A) to match the UML and template usage.

issues.description: The problem statement (and the template Main) describe and use a Rideable.messageOnRide() method with no parameters, but the solution defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) and updates Pig/Seal accordingly. This changes the conceptual method signature and return content (adds speed and "at X mph"), causing a mismatch: student code based on the problem/template (calling messageOnRide() with no argument) will not compile against the solution implementation and the intended behavior described in the task.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Rideable.messageOnRide signature across artifacts. Preferably revert the solution to match the problem/template by changing Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) to messageOnRide() and update Pig/Seal implementations to return the text exactly as specified in the task ("Riding on [Animal Type] [name]"). Alternatively, update the problem statement and template examples to require a speed parameter and adjust the described return value to include speed, but ensure all three artifacts use the same method signature.
